data.narrative:
Stellaria is a seed-stage nuclear energy company founded by Nicolas Breyton and backed by CEA and Schneider Electric. The company has raised €23M to date. The nuclear energy sector contains 11 comparable companies: 3 public (OKLO, NNE, SMR) and 8 private peers including Nano Nuclear Energy, Oklo, X-Energy, Fuse Energy, and Applied Atomics.

Standard peer-median valuation cannot be reliably applied to Stellaria. The nuclear energy peer set, while populated with 11 total comparables, lacks sufficient same-stage or adjacent-stage companies with similar valuation tier characteristics. Only one same-stage and one adjacent-stage peer were identified, falling short of the minimum three-datapoint threshold required for statistical relevance. A broad sector median would introduce material noise given the heterogeneity in business models and development timelines across the nuclear sector.

Given the data constraints, this valuation requires alternative approaches beyond peer multiples—such as cost-of-capital methods, scenario-based DCF analysis tied to regulatory and deployment milestones, or venture-backed funding round benchmarking within the clean energy capital markets. The key uncertainties remain regulatory pathway clarity, technology differentiation within modular nuclear, and the timing of capital deployment relative to sector maturation. Additional data on recent private funding rounds and technology-specific risk profiles would strengthen any range recommendation.
